note: How many plan units one percent of the WEEKLY plan limit is, and how heavily each model's tokens count against it, as DATA (like model-tiers.json: a number baked into code goes stale silently). Read by hooks/lib/plan-allowance.mjs (the `BUDGET: N%` spawn note and its 80% / 100% notices), scripts/allowance.mjs (an agent's own spend) and scripts/lib/daily-checkup.mjs (the daily checkup and the usage analysis: its model weights). Override without a release by writing a file of this shape to <state root>/plan-weights.json (the same place as the model-tiers.json override; merged by key, one level deep, so a file naming only models.opus.weight keeps everything else). Every figure carries its date, source, interval and status: 'measured' (fitted from the operator's own official readings), 'assumed' (a stand-in, not fitted) or 'estimated' (derived from a neighbouring cell). Nothing here is a published limit.

unit.description: A plan unit is a token count priced at the Sonnet 5 vector, then times the model's weight: input 1, output 5, cache write 1.25 (5 minute) or 2 (1 hour), cache read 0.1 (times cacheReadFactor), all times inPerMTok/1e6.

unitsPerPercent.source: Weight fit of 2026-11-03: 107 official weekly readings (2026-10-02 to 2026-11-03) against 502,767 requests from local transcripts. Three independent weeks gave 28.4, 28.8 and 28.5 units per 1% at Opus 1.5 and cache reads at API price.

cacheReadFactor.source: Same fit. Cache reads counted at API price (1.0). The fit mildly prefers 0.5 to 0.75 (residual 86.5 and 87.5 against 101.6 at 1.0) but readings inside a window are serially correlated, so the preference is not conclusive. Kept at 1.0; at 0.5 the Opus weight fits 1.10 and units per percent 17.5, so the two must move together.

sonnet.source: Defined as 1.0; every other weight is relative to it.

opus.source: Weight fit of 2026-11-03, bootstrap of 107 readings at cache reads priced 1.0 (90% interval). The in-app tooltip says 1.5, inside the interval.

haiku.source: API price ratio. The fit gave 0.29 +-0.38 to 0.68 +-0.47, not distinguishable from 0 to 1.

fable.source: Weight fit of 2026-11-03: 2.3 +-0.8 (cache reads at half price) to 3.2 +-1.1 (API price) on the weekly meter, from only 548 Fable requests (7 in the current week). Unreliable, so a rough guide (+-1). The 5x API price ratio is not what the meter showed.

perCall.description: Median plan cost of ONE model call (one API request, main thread and subagents together) as a percent of the weekly limit, by model and effort, from transcripts since 2026-10-02. It is dominated by cache reads of the loaded context, so it moves little with effort. Each model's cells were computed at basisWeight; the reader rescales them by weight / basisWeight so a changed weight moves the call estimate with it. A cell marked in 'estimated' is not measured: the reader falls back to the nearest effort of the same model.
perCall.source: Weight fit of 2026-11-03, section 4: median % of weekly per call from 100% of calls since 2026-10-02 (sonnet 6.9k to 56.6k calls per effort, opus 19k to 63k, haiku 1.8k, fable 353). Opus low is n=60; haiku high and xhigh and fable high are on assumed weights.
perCall.medianTokensSource: Median TOTAL tokens per call (input + output + cache write + cache read, one API request, main thread and subagents together) from the same 502,767-request scan of 2026-11-03 (usage-weight-fit-detail.md section 4), same calls and same cut (since 2026-10-02) as medianPct: sonnet 6.9k to 56.6k calls per effort, opus 19k to 63k (low n=60), haiku 0.5k to 1.8k, fable 353. Recomputed by taking the median of in + out + cw5 + cw1 + cr over each model x effort cell of requests.jsonl. A call is mostly cache reads of the loaded context, so the figure moves little with effort. A cell in 'estimated' has no tokens of its own either: the reader falls back to the nearest effort of the same model, as for medianPct. The note multiplies the calls an allowance buys (allowance / medianPct) by this median to say how many tokens that is at the agent's typical mix.
perCall.mainThreadNote: A main-thread call costs about 1.6 to 1.8 times a subagent call at equal effort (a bigger context). The cells mix both; a lead planning its own work should expect the higher end.
